batch._note: Milestone 657 (docs/PLAN_CITY_DRAWS.md): the centre's opaque, lit materials without detail maps written in batches over texture arrays at these sizes (tools/import-city.ts writePack, src/game/neonbatch.ts): one primitive a batch, each vertex its material's row in a table, each material's pictures a layer of an array a kind. The centre was 441 primitives, one a material, each spanning the whole city, all drawn whichever way a camera looked: about 420 draw calls a frame from the street, the frame's largest cost on a laptop's processor (the lobby agent's measure). `capMB`: no array past this many bytes at a byte a pixel and its mips (128 MB, the least single allocation Direct3D 11 promises), and none past 255 materials and a neutral layer (WebGL 2 promises 256 layers): lo one batch, hi three, max twelve. Measured at lo: 249 materials in one batch, 441 primitives to 193, the look unchanged at 12 spots; half a processor 40 to 50 fps, the whole one 132 to 139. Cutting the batches into 50 m cells was tried and dropped: from the street most cells are in view (5% fewer triangles) and it bought no fps.

Z -10.1 is the south edge: from there the pack's own balcony and curb stand at 7 and 10.5 m (boxes z -10 to -9.5, 7 to 8.35 and 10.5 to 11.25), which are its rail. The court under the ground slab is not opened: its ceiling carries the plaza's own walks to the lobby, and the review's other half is met from the hall. A rail needs a floor a body can reach; none along the flights' arrivals. `flight`: the pack's Stairs01c, 3 m wide over yellow parapets and 1.92 m of glass, the widest straight flight in the bundle: 0.2 m at its foot, slope 0.7, 3.65 m at its ridge, 3.56 at its end, read off the model, so it stands `sink` in the floor, `treads` of `climb` / 16 m, risers 22 cm; `lanes` north of the middle, as the crate at (-11, -15.2), a ground floor draw that must not move, stands 0.5 m off the first flight's foot on its south side and stopped a lane at 0.6. RampStairsLarge00 (5 by 15 m, a double ramp, rises 3.5 m) was measured and fits this band only with its landing through the tower's lower block and rises one storey for 62 m2 of slab. The facade over it is a 3 m storey, its glass 45.94 to 48.06 m and the next row's from 48.92, so the lid's underside is clear of the glass at 48.1 m, a 2.6 m ceiling, and its top, `at`, 5 cm under the facade's next floor line, 48.5 m, where the pack has a ledge in the west face's groove (RoundedPlasticPanel00) that a lid topped at 48.5 lay in one plane with (1.6 m2); `slab` 0.35 m thick. Its inside is found in the facade's solid band round it, `band` (48.12 to 48.9 m, between the storey's glass and the next row's, measured off the model): from standing height up the facade is the hollow's glass.

Not measured for a seal as the new floors are: their balconies open out of the shell at standing height, the way onto them, and a ray out onto a balcony is no gap.

A level's `floor.skirts`: its own inside wall in bands round its edge, metres over its floor, between its window rows (the shell's round windows 0.75 to 2.1 m over the floor, the loft's again at 3.75 to 5.1): the pack's shell is drawn from outside, and the photographs showed slivers of sky between its trims at the floor's foot, under the ceiling and between the loft's rows.

Not to the crown: a rope's top end throws a rider 3.7 m on whichever way they face, and between the crown's 0.9 m parapet and the spire's ring round the stair the crown has bands 4 to 6.5 m wide, so riders facing the near edge went over it; the crown is the stair's and its two pads'. `at` each in the building's own frame (the middles of the NW and SE rooms, 3 m and more from every wall: a rider is put off the top 3.7 m on whichever way they face, and the first south-east one, 2 m from the east wall, was bounced back onto its barrier), a `hole` square round it through every slab it passes, from `hang` over the floor (a lift's, 2.234) to `over` over the penthouse's floor (a lift's 2.5, under its ceiling), in `colour`. `rail`: a low barrier, the pack's 0.64 m street fence (its top 0.54 m over the floor, past a body's 0.46 m step), round each hole on each level, `off` from the rope with its inner face outside the hole: a body walking the floor is not dropped down the shaft, and a rider put off the top or jumping off at a level clears it.

rules._collision: How the bake builds the map's collision boxes from its drawn pieces (tools/import-neon.ts, tools/import-city.ts districtSolids): `cell` metres a column, faces within `stick` of a column's edge counted in it, nothing below `floor`, columns within `merge` of a height joined, a face thinner than `thin` thickened, and no box topping out under `minTop`. The cypresses in their planters (GardenPit_premade00d, 01b and 02c: their pits the same Box045 parts) collide the same way since Milestone 585: solid to their 11 to 15 m tops, a body climbed one by running into it (SpeedKills' climb) and stood on its crown.

rules._arenas: The two 1v1 arenas (neon-layout.ts, the owner 2026-10-09: "2 1v1 maps ... the 1v1 maps are supposed to be super basic"): small walled rooms of the bundle's own pieces, `at` (map-local, their middle) out past the city's square, where nothing of the city stands, each its own `chunk` (not "c-": the bake keeps it a node of its own, drawn alone while it is played and hidden in a battle royale). `half` the room's inside half widths (x, z) to the walls' inner faces, the page's bounds; `floor` tiled over it, drawn only (the world's floor is the ground); `walls` a row of `piece` every `long` m along each side, `thick` through, at each height in `rows`, `top` high (`front` the way the face wanted inside looks unturned, and each side turned so it looks into the room: the yard's street wall is drawn from one side only, and turned alike on both sides of the yard, one side of it was not there; the hall's panels are concrete one side and plaster the other, and turned alike, two of its walls were plaster: the concrete in, as its pillars), the upper row's panels `windows.at` on `windows.sides` that piece instead; `roof` tiled as the floor, its underside at `y`; `lamps` (the hall's are the base's ceiling lamp, so the fill lights stand under them) and `signs` [piece, x, z, y] turned to the middle; `pillars` and `cover` [piece, x, z, yaw, y] laid twice, the second half a turn about the middle, so neither end is the better; `spawns` one of each opposite pair (the second is its half turn), each facing the middle, and none within `clear` m of the cover, nor the middle's circle (3.5 m) within it; `zones` Control's three points, the first the 1v1's circle; `shadow` the sun's shadow box's half width over it, its room and a margin (range.ts setShadowRegion). NEON YARD is open to the sky in 7 m concrete walls, its cover crates, cool boxes and a 3 m wall across each end; NEON HALL a closed hall under a 6 m roof, six pillars, crates and a wall before each end. The line between each pair of opposite spawns is broken by a wall at least 6 m in front of each, so a spawn faces open floor (the e2e's arenas' rule) and the middle's circle is clear (tools/checks/sk-neon.ts). THE GULAG (Milestone 662) is a third, played only as the Gulag's fight (br.json gulag.map): `floor.mat` a material over its tiles, `centre` what stands in its middle, laid as the cover is but not held clear of the middle, and `ways` where a bot starts up it.

list._note: THE GULAG (Milestone 662; the owner, 2026-10-18: "the gulag should just be one street like the firing range with one building in the middle, a super simple one, or just a ledge that has two levels to it and can see the rest of the gulag when they are on top, just a double jump height worth"). One street 48 by 15 m between concrete walls, laid as the city's straight streets are: a 10 m road of asphalt down the middle (`floor`, its `road`), a pavement 2.5 m wide either side (`pave`), a kerb along each edge of the road (`kerb`, the city's); the city's street lamps along both kerbs and a sign on each end wall. In its middle the ledge (`centre`, its west half given and the east the same turned about the middle): a lower level 16 by 6 m with its top at 1.4 m, and on it an upper block 6 by 6 m with its top at 2.7 m: a jump (1.42 m, movement.json jumpHeight) from the street to the lower level and from it to the top, and a jump and a double jump (1.32 m more, 2.74 m) from the street to the top on its long sides, no mantle needed. A standing eye on the top, 4.4 m up, sees over every piece of cover in the street but the wall before each spawn. Bots neither jump nor climb, and the Gulag's fight is against a bot, so two of the pack's simple stairs side by side climb each end to the lower level and two more climb from it to the top (each stair 1.92 m, its foot sunk in what it stands on: 0.52 m under the street, 0.62 m into the lower level); a bot going for the top walks to `ways`, a metre out from the end stairs' foot on the street's long axis, and straight up from there (brmatch.ts gulagFrame). The overtime flag is the ledge's top (zones' first, the middle), and the layout writes the top's height under it to cfg.arenas.gulag.ledge. The corners of each block closed with the pack's half-metre wall. Cover in each half, laid twice as every arena's is: a wall by each spawn, a stack of two crates, a cooling unit and a vending machine against the wall.

The signs at `signs.scale` times the pack's size (Milestone 670, round 3: 'small and unlit by day').

Each along between two blade signs (they stand every 8 m), so none crosses one.

works._note: THE WORKS (Milestone 646), the south-east district past the ring road in THE WELL's sector, the one crossed indoors: an L of halls of the pack's rusted metal walls, its south arm along z 115 to 145 and its east arm along x 115 to 145, the corner square's works block between. Each hall a `box` [x0, x1, z0, z1], `storeys` of `storey` metres, its walls the pack's 10 and 5 m rusted panels (`wall`, `wallShort`, 0.32 m thick) drawn only on the bake's typed collision, each with a twin turned about on its footprint (the panels are faced on one side only), laid in 5 m modules from each corner; `doors` on each side ([n]orth z0, [s]outh z1, [w]est x0, [e]ast x1) by their middles, each `door` metres wide and the ground storey's full height, the middles on the bots' street node lines so a node stands in each doorway: down each arm's middle (z 125, x 125) through the end walls, in from the ring road and out to the edge through the sides. Its roof the pack's floor tiles (`roof`, largest first) over a typed slab `slab` thick; the ceiling lamp the game lights as fill (`lamp`) under it every `lampEvery` metres each way, so a hall is lit inside. The 10 m between halls are yards, a footbridge's span. Its name (`name`) in THE WELL's teal on the south arm's second hall, over its wall beside the ring road's door.

In the bake the pack's stair collides between stringers standing 0.15 to 0.4 m over its treads, a lane about 1 m wide (measured off the bake: the up flight between own x 0.25 and 1.75, the return between -1.5 and 0), and a 0.81 m body walking up a little off its middle caught on one: the owner's "i can glitch through stairs all the time when going up" (2026-10-12). Each flight `treads` steps over `run` metres from the front edge (own z 0) back to the landing, half the piece's `rise` a flight; `up` and `down` each flight's own x range from stringer to stringer, `landing` its box (own x0, x1, z0, z1) at half the rise; a guard `guard` metres over each step and `thick` wide along each flight's sides and between them, so nobody walks off one. `route` a body's way up it in its own metres and height (the base's and the hotel's, measured off its parts), and `lanes` the own x a check walks each flight up at: its middle and as near each side as a body's 0.41 m half width lets it go.

So the pieces stand on the middle, round the way down and 2.1 m and more from it: the pack's tall utility cabinet (4.7 m) at its south-east corner, over a standing eye, an AC unit (1.96 m) at its south-west and the pack's cooling plant (1.5 m) on its north ledge, a chest-high piece to whoever holds the middle against the north apron where the pad and the north rope arrive. The rope riders' ways clear: the south rope's carries its riders north along x 8.5 to 10 past its top (the AC's columns start at x 9.0 at 50.5 m, over a rider's 49.7 m feet only where the raised middle's own face already stops one), the east rope's along z -5.5 to -4.5, the north rope's along x 11 to 13.7 into the middle's north face.
highCover._decks1048: Milestone 1048, `deck-n`, `deck-s`, `deck-w`, `deck-e` (the centre's fifteenth reviews, picture 14: 'the High City roof a bare disc', 'AC units and sign frames', 'stair houses, plant, tanks, cover sets'): each deck the pack's roof stair house (RoofEndRoom03, 3 by 3 m, 4.25 m, its door turned to the deck's middle), a plant (the north deck the pack's water tank on its lattice stand, BuildingTank05, 7.5 m, solid to 4 m square under a 5 m tank from 3 m up; the other three the pack's 4.7 m utility cabinet: on the south and east decks every cell open enough for the tank carries a bots' link, and on the west deck the tank, tried in its west lobe, closed the lobe's neck to the w-out pad's landing in the decks' walk check), an AC unit (Coolbox01d Variant, 1.96 m), a sign frame (AD_Structure02, 9.14 m, its lit face to the tower but on the north deck, where the landmark tank stands between, to the north) and a crate stack (two of the gangway's crates and a third on them, 2 m). The disc of picture 14 is the north deck's south lobe, the deck's arrivals: the n-in pad's landing, the lookout rope's end and the glass lift's top all stand within 6 m of each other there, so it keeps no piece; the pieces stand on the deck's arms and lobes behind the picture's camera. Measured off version 131, footprint to mark as the map check measures: the nearest a piece stands to a deck pad's landing 6.1 m, a zip's end 4.7 m, a bridge's end 5.0 m, a glass lift's top 11.75 m; from its columns at a body's height to the deck's own perches and landmark 0.9 m and more.
highCover._gangway1049: Milestone 1049, `gangway` (the centre's fifteenth reviews, picture 25: 'cover on one rail only', 'one crate stack'): the gangway's own six sets alternate rails 7 m apart, each with its shield, so from any spot the nearer rail's cover hid the far one's. Three cooling plants (Coolbox01, 1.5 m) against the north rail and three crate stacks (2 m) against the south, each opposite the other rail's shield and never opposite a set: x 23.5, 37.5 and 50.5 north, 16.5, 30.5 and 44.5 south. Each rail then has cover past a crouch no more than 6.4 m apart (measured on the sets' and shields' own boxes and the new pieces' footprints), and the narrowest lane between the rails at a body's height is 2.0 m (the bake's columns: the plants' at z 4.5 to 5.5, the stacks' at 7.0 to 8.0, against the deck's middle line at 6.125; the stacks stand 0.125 m off the south glass where the sets stand 0.15 so their half-metre columns start at 7.0, as at 7.475 they reached 6.5 and left a 1 m slot, which the bridges' walk check's body does not pass). highCover._canyon1050: Milestone 1050, `canyon` (the districts' ninth reviews, picture d21: 'acres of flat brown with a few tanks and screens', 'stepped roofs with stair houses, tank stands, billboard frames'): five stair houses, four water tanks on their stands, three sign frames (their lit faces north, to the canyon and the city's middle), three crate stacks and two AC units over the roofs at 26.86 m, among the payoffs' decks and sheds and the perches, each in a cell of the bots' 5 m lines of roof nodes or cutting only a cell's diagonal. roofs._note: Milestones 1047 to 1050's map check (tools/checks/sk-neon.ts, 'the roofs dressed'): `groups` the least pieces each group of rows lays; `tall` a piece over a standing eye (1.7 m) with a hand to spare, so it breaks a sightline across its roof; `decks` the kinds each High City deck has (`plant` either), `canyon` how many of each THE CANYON has. `keep` the metres a piece's footprint keeps off each way onto a roof: `pad` a High City deck pad's landing (3 m in, rules.perches_clear.pad's 4), `lift` a glass lift's top (a rider steps off at speed), `zip` a deck end of a zip line (rules.perches_clear.zip's 4), `zipTop` a lookout end of one (rules.low.zip.lookout.clear), `bridge` a bridge's end, its stair and its mouth, `landing` the landing of every other pad up (2.5 to 3.5 m past its wall's face: the lookout's raised middle itself stands 2.1 m from the top pad's), `downPad` the lookout's way down (squad.json pad.reach), `crossing` each end of THE CANYON's crossings, `lamp` its roof lamps. `high` cover past a crouched body (1.19 m) and a hand, on the gangway; `every` the longest stretch of either rail bare of it; `lane` the narrowest lane between its rails at a body's height (a body 0.81 m and the bridges' walk check's cells); `walk` the gangway walked from past the window's cell to short of the corner (metres in from each end of its long leg) and the lookout's floor from the top pad's landing to each end of its horseshoe; `shield` the half-size panel and its faces' material; `coping` the tower's material on the lookout's rim.

sites._landmarks: Milestone 661, from the map's gap analysis (docs/GAP_ANALYSIS_MAP.md): Hyper Scape puts its best and fastest-respawning loot in its landmarks (Red Tiger), Apex in its high-tier places and vaults, and that is why a squad drops on one place over another. The eight districts each had a landmark and no loot of their own beyond their sector's spread; each now has a site there (`landmark`), rolled at loot.json's `landmark` tier: its courtyard, top tier, hall, hotel, deck, club, market or block hall, `reach` metres round `at`, on its own floor `y` where it has one (the capsule hotel's galleries are all its floors).

game._flatten1069: Milestone 1069 (the eighteenth reviews, all four, and the four of the round before: 'the asphalt a blotchy cloud texture', 'looks like carpet', 'brown mud with blue stains', 18, 22, d01, d13b, d22): `flatten`, a pack material's main map pulled toward its own mean, `keep` of its contrast left, its derived wears too (src/game/neonmap.ts). Asphalt00's main map is Noise00, a cloud noise there to break its detail's repeat. Shot from 22 and 18 with the game's own materials changed in the page: its normals off, it matt, and its main map off; only the last cleared the blotches, and with it off the detail's 0.5 m repeat showed as a grid and the road lightened to 0.33. At `keep` 0.35 the blotches are gone and the repeat still broken (0.15 showed the grid). `mean` the main map's own, its linear values' mean (0.553, off a 256 by 256 sample of Noise00.png), so the road's tone holds, the map check measuring it again.
game._anisotropy1063: Milestone 1063 (the seventeenth reviews of the centre and the eleventh of the districts, all four, and the round before: 'the ground at the district mouths smeared brown or blue noise', d01, d13b, d22, the WORKS hall floor d23; 'blotchy low-res asphalt', 18, 22): every texture of the city's file was drawn with the loader's default of one sample, so a surface seen at a slant, a street a few metres out, read a mip level as coarse as its steepest axis asked, many times coarser along the street than across it, and smeared. Each texture the file draws, its own maps, its detail maps and its batches' arrays, now takes `anisotropy` samples along the slant by the kit the preset draws (lo the Competitive preset's, hi Balanced's, max High's), never more than the device's own cap. Few on lo, the preset for frames.
game._fill: The interiors' fill (neonmap.ts updateNeonFill): a fixed pool of `count` point lights on High, `byPreset` on the others (each light is in every lit shader per pixel on every preset, a cost on laptops: the lobby's frame-time pass, 2026-10-03), no shadows, each frame at the `count` lamp spots nearest the eye within `reach` m, height counted `tall` times over so a storey's own lamps come first (the floor above's, through a slab, lit nothing you could see); the spots are the pack's ceiling lamps the layout hung in the base and the tower, `under` m below the fitting, and a grid every `every` m over the court's and the station's floors `height` m up, none within `off` m of anything solid. `intensity` is three.js's candela (`tower` for the tower's floors' own lamps: their storeys are 3 m, the lamps close together and a metre over the eye under pale ceilings, and at the base's 60 they drew white, a mean luminance of 0.62 to 0.80 of full and up to a third of the picture clipped, where the court is 0.51 with nothing clipped; measured at 60, 24, 12 and 6, and 12 brings them to 0.27 to 0.51 with a few per cent clipped, the second review, 2026-10-03), `distance` where a light's reach ends, `colour` the lamps' warm white. The tower's floors, the base's storeys and the court drew near black at noon with only the sky's ambient (docs/CENTRE_REVIEW.md, 2026-10-02).
